Title: Provision of Continuous Attitude Surveys to Defence Medical Services
Description:
The Headquarters Surgeon General  is responsible for conducting the Defence Medical Services (DMS) Continuous Attitude Surveys (CAS).  Surveys are conducted for serving military DMS personnel (both regular and reserve) employed within the MOD.  They are used to provide management information to the Defence Medical Services Board and the Personnel Policy Working Group.

As part of various initiatives within the DMS, the key research objective is to identify areas for development that can help inform future HR strategic policy decisions across DMS, including the single Services Medical; Branches.

The Supplier is required to:
1. Produce and deliver, using the most appropriate means, a self-completion questionnaire for on average approximately 10,000 military medical personnel to complete with a method of return to the Contractor within an agreed timeline.  The questionnaire should contain no more than 100 attitudinal questions, 5 non-standard questions, 12 demographic questions and up to four opportunities for open comments.  The sample strategy will be directed by the Designated Officer (DO).

2. Conduct statistical and trend analysis from results over a 3-year period (2016 - 2018).

3.  Provide final reports in hard copy format (2 copies) and soft copy format (1 copy) and data analysis comparator tool in electronic format (licences for 3 people to access the tool) to the DO, 3 weeks prior to the results presentation. 

4. Produce PowerPoint presentations of headline results in a house style agreed between the Contractor and the DO for up to four presentations.  These presentations will then form the verbal feedback from the Contractor to the Authority. 

5. Provide up to 6 days on-site support to the Authority during the survey period to assist with the administration of the survey.

Title: ISS Service Integration Partner (SIP)
Description:
ISS is the organisation within the Ministry of Defence (the "Authority") responsible for delivering the Defence Information Strategy, through the design, development and operation of information and communication technology ("ICT") across the Authority. In line with this strategy, ISS is moving away from current high-value and complex contracts to a more cost-efficient 'Defence as a Platform' ("DaaP") model. 

The DaaP model will enable ISS to move from the current high-value and complex contracts to a more cost-efficient platform model with common architecture across all services, enabling smaller and more agile contracts to be placed. The DaaP contract structure will also involve suppliers of DaaP services working together collaboratively. This requirement will be supported by a binding collaboration agreement which will set out a range of objectives and principles designed to encourage and facilitate collaboration among suppliers. 

The DaaP model also anticipates that ISS will build upon its existing in-house DaaP Services Integration Office ("DSIO"). The DSIO is a core team that manages, tracks and intervenes in ISS projects and programmes for the delivery of, and changes to, specific ICT services ("ISS Projects") in order to ensure overall integration and coherence of ISS ICT services. DSIO also ensures that any incoherencies with delivering end-to-end ISS ICT services are appropriately identified, documented and managed. 

SIP role and responsibilities 

The Authority now wishes to procure an ISS Service Integration Partner (SIP) to support DSIO and bring about the step-change in capability required to deliver the full benefits of the DaaP model, and manage an increasingly complex multi-sourcing service landscape. 

The SIP will augment and support the DSIO to ensure the requisite integration and coherence of the design, development and delivery of all DaaP services, through multiple transition states and ultimately into live service. 

This will include (without limitation) the SIP delivering the following services to ISS and the Authority: 

a) delivering and maintaining a transparent, robust and coherent transition state model to ensure the viable delivery of ISS services; 

b) ensuring all multi-sourced components of the Authority's ICT estate are integrated and remain coherent throughout the complete service development lifecycle, supporting the delivery of end-to-end ISS services that meet the Authority's expectations and designated performance levels for ISS Services; 

c) supporting a 'one team' approach for the delivery of ISS services where all parties collaborate effectively and work towards shared outcomes; and 

d) delivering a comprehensive knowledge transfer, upskilling and training programme to ensure that the DSIO is able to perform such service integration activities in-house in the future.

Title: Provision of Emergency Airfield Cover for Boscombe Down Aerodrome
Description:
Emergency Medical provision required

Within 10 Minutes  of an emergency call the contractor will provide:

Airfield Incident

a.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

Off-Site Incident

b.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

Domestic Incident on Boscombe Down

c.	Pre-Hospital emergency medical cover to preserve lives as safely as possible by providing triage, live-saving first aid, Basic Life Support and Advanced Life Support, until the casualties can receive the advanced trauma response and onward casualty transfer provided through the NHS ambulance service. In conjunction with the fire service and under the command of the Fire Master. 

The Emergency Medical Airfield cover

This will consist of several elements including:

a.	Provision of Pre-Hospital Emergency Care and Treatment.
b.	Participation in all on and off (as determined by the exercise and training plans in conjunction with DPHC) site exercising and training events as directed by the Fire Master.
c.	Participation in the creation and generation of paramedic and technician response to major incident plans for the Airfield at MOD Boscombe Down as directed by the Fire Master.
d.	Regular review session with the Military Aviation Medical Examiner (MAME) Medical Officer responsible for MOD Boscombe Down based at the Bulford Medical Centre. 
e.	Support to the airfield in the management of aircraft and air personnel first aid kits destruction.

Organisation Name: Ministry of Defence, DSTL, Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (DSTL)
Title: SERAPIS Framework
Description:
In order to maximise the impact of Science and Technology (S&T) for the Defence and Security (D&S) of the UK, Dstl's role includes the responsibility for leading the formulation, design and delivery of a coherent and integrated Ministry of Defence (MOD) S&T programme using industrial, academic and government resources. In particular, the Cyber and Information Systems Division stewards both the Cyber and the Command, Control, Communications, Computer, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities (including Space).  The Defence and Security Analysis Division stewards the Synthetic Environment and Simulation capabilities.
      
      The Serapis Framework aims to provide an expedient mechanism for Dstl to access industrial and academic expertise both within the UK and wider, in support of the Divisions' S&T programmes, and potentially wider MOD and Partner Across Government organisations (PAGs). The construct should allow the supply base to be refreshed throughout the contract lifespan, ensuring that Dstl has access to innovative solutions and robust technical support. Such a construct will allow for the rapid response to emerging capability needs, Urgent Operational Requirements / Urgent Capability Requirements (UOR / UCR) and surge requirements emanating from operations.
      
      Based on the structure and contents of the programmes and the aggregation of wider requirements across the portfolios, the Serapis Framework has been categorised into six Lots, details of each Lot is provided in this notice.
      
      The competition is seeking to appoint a Prime Contractor for each Lot to lead, manage and deliver research in to the areas covered by the six Lots.  The appointed Prime Contractors will be responsible for delivering agile, and cutting-edge research, building and maintaining a robust supplier network with an emphasis on scientific excellence, innovation, and collaboration to exploit research, skills and capabilities. 
      
      In addition to Dstl and the Ministry of Defence (MOD), the Serapis Framework will be available to the following Government Departments / Public Authorities (including their agencies and public bodies): the Home Office, the Foreign & Commonwealth Office and the Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy.

Title: GB-Gloucester: MOD Medal Laser Engraving Machines - Purchase Option-No.2
Description:
The MOD Medals Office has a requirement for two compact pulsed fibre laser engraving machines and two PCs with screens, keyboards and appropriate software to operate the machines in accordance with the specification. Please note that the MOD have also placed a Contract Notice advertising this requirement as an option to have two engraving machines provided as a service. The requirement is also for the installation of the equipment, operator training and a preventative maintenance and support package to cover the laser engraving machines, the PC hardware and software and which will include a Customer Helpline with availability from 08.00 to 16.30, Mon to Fri. 
      The laser engraving machines will be required to:
      •   engrave a range of medals and awards made from a variety of metals including but not limited to Sterling Silver, Cupro Nickel and Rhodium plated Cupro Nickel;
      •   engrave centrally around the rim of circular and oval medals with thicknesses that range between 3mm and 6mm; 
      •   engrave both flat and concave surfaces in both straight lines and circles without damaging the surfaces of the medals:
      •   engrave between 25 and 30 circular and oval medals per hour and work for approx. 8 hours per day (upto 6 days a week);
      •   engrave details provided on a USB stick as a delimited text file and or a xml file (.csv would not be acceptable as the "comma" would be included in the engraving details).
      Full details of the requirement can be found in the Statement of Requirement which is contained in the Invitation To Tender (ITT) Document which is available under the supporting documents on Defence Contracts Online (DCO) (see www.contracts.mod.uk) and can be accessed from the Response Manager page using - Access Code 9U46NRU95T.
      
      MOD plan to hold a Bidders Conference on Mon 20 May at 12:00 at Imjin Barracks, Innsworth, Gloucester (unfortunately we are not able to provide lunch) any suppliers interested in attending should email James.Davies206@mod.gov.uk with the names of those who will be attending (please limit this to 2 attendees) by 11:00 Thu 16 May 2019.
      
      Suppliers interested in this requirement should complete Parts 1 and 2 of the on-line Suitability Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) including the Declaration using the DCO and submit it electronically by 11:00 on Thu 30/05/2019. Suppliers should also complete their tender, as detailed in the ITT Document under supporting documents on the DCO and should also submit it (via post or courier) to arrive by 11:00 on Thu 30/05/2019. The SAQ details the grounds for rejecting Requests to Participate and the minimum levels of capacity and capability that are required to perform the contract.
      
      The full Selection and Award Criteria can be found in the ITT document at Section D on page 9. Please note that in order for a tender to be evaluated the tenderer must first complete the SAQ as detailed above.

Title: DInfoCom/0069 - Provision of Digital Project Support for Armed Forces Recruiting Programme
Description:

The Programme started life in March 2018 as an Army programme; the Defence Board directed that AFRP become Tri-Service in December 2018.
